notes:
Summary: Mariner runs a low-latency reranking pipeline for RT ad auctions; firing ~250k requests/min pre-aggregation. Evaluating Redwood Dedicated for predictable unit economics and latency stability. Top negotiation topics: guaranteed min tokens/sec, hard concurrency caps per-GPU, allowed burst policy (short bursts vs sustained), and fallback model tiers for graceful degradation.

Call highlights: - 2026-02-11 discovery with Janelle + infra lead: outlined workload (rerank + light chat for support agents). Asked for 'hard' p99 SLOs and a minimum tokens/sec guarantee during business hours.
- 2026-02-25 technical deep-dive: SE provided latency/throughput model; customer pushed back on GPU overcommit scenarios; wants explicit per-device concurrency limits.
- 2026-03-05 procurement + legal: discussed SLA credit formula; legal requests explicit wording on burst handling and how Redwood counts tokens for billing during bursts.

Customer quotes: "We need a floor—if the product promises throughput we can't be the ones to absorb variance." — Janelle W.

Internal context: Finance modelling shows sensitivity to token-rate floors; pricing needs to include a capped burst allowance (e.g., 20% sustained for 5 minutes, 100% micro-burst for 30s) or a two-tiered charge. SE recommends RB sizing: reserve 8x A100-equivalent GPUs for peak and 4x for baseline with autoscaling stripe for bursts. Ops note: prefer VPC private control plane and KMS integration.

POC ask: 2-week dedicated evaluation in us-west with a defined traffic replay (dataset id: mt-replay-0301). Must include telemetry: per-token latency histograms, per-GPU concurrency charts, and token accounting log.

Negotiation sweet spots: minimum tokens/sec floor (target 1,200,000 tokens/min -> ~20k tokens/sec) with a 20% guaranteed headroom during business hours, concurrency cap per GPU 6-8 concurrent requests for long-context rerank flows, burst policy: 100% micro-burst allowance up to 30s per minute, sustained burst capped at 20% for up to 5 minutes before fallback routing triggers.

Risks: If Redwood enforces strict concurrency caps without efficient batching/eviction, p99 latency may spike. Legal insists on a rollback clause if fallback logic causes >0.5% request loss during bursts.

requirements_summary: Workload: reranking (short context) + high-throughput embeddings for lookups
Min throughput target: 1,200,000 tokens/min (20k tokens/sec) as contractual floor
Latency SLOs: p50 < 50ms, p95 < 120ms, p99 < 250ms under guaranteed baseline
Concurrency policy: per-GPU hard cap 6-8 requests for long-context rerank; system should support higher concurrency with batching for short-ctx embedding calls
Burst policy: micro-burst 100% allowed up to 30s; sustained burst max 20% for up to 5 minutes before fallback to cheaper model or region
Model preferences: quantized Llama-family variants for cost, fallback to smaller r2-like family for degraded mode
Telemetry: token-level accounting, per-request latency, per-GPU utilization charts, audit logs for billing reconciliation
po_caveats: Will not sign until legal accepts burst clause + rollback language. Finance requires an ARR uplift cap tied to model family changes. Wants explicit monthly true-up clause for token overages.
pricing_notes: Customer prefers flat reserved capacity with a guaranteed token floor; proposals include (A) baseline reserve + burst bucket billing, (B) tiered pricing by model family with higher token multiplier for high-recall variants. Finance asked Redwood for a modeled cost breakdown with 95th percentile token usage included.
technical_constraints: Must run in us-west with VPC peering; no egress of raw request payload to shared services; HSM/KMS for key material; offline attestation doc required. On-prem option acceptable for future air-gapped requirements.
